text:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: SEV1: kv-cache service in us-east-2 reporting sustained NCCL stalls + paging spikes. Auto-escalating to platform on-call. metrics: https://internal.metrics/redwood/kv-cache?panel=nccL_and_paging

rachel: I'm awake, grabbing traces. noticed a sudden increase in page-in from NVMe and per-GPU allreduce times.

tom: recent change: tensor-split allocator introduced a new 'min_chunk_strategy' to reduce fragmentation (deployed 2026-03-16 04:11 UTC, commit a9b2f1). it can produce zero-sized shards on rare key distributions -> causes rank imbalance and frequent NCCL retries.

priya: if ranks are idling waiting on allreduce it'll pile up continuous batching and KV cache insertion backlog -> cache blowup and paging. we should throttle the batching window asap.

rachel: applying emergency knob: set CONT_BATCH_WINDOW_MS=0 and KV_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES=200000 for region us-east-2 via runtime admin API.

rachel: ```bash
# emergency mitigations
curl -X POST https://admin.internal/runtime/config -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"region":"us-east-2","kv_cache": {"continuous_batch_window_ms": 0, "max_entries": 200000}, "tp": {"alloc_min_chunk": 256}}'

# bump NCCL env to be slightly more tolerant (temporary)
kubectl set env deploy/kv-shard -n runtime NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0 NCCL_TIMEOUT=60 -l region=us-east-2
```

rachel: knobs flipped at 1775000035. paging rate started falling. nvme latency still elevated on 2 nodes.

dan: which nodes are hot? I'll pull NVMe SMART and kernel logs.

dan: hot nodes: us-east2-gpu-07 and us-east2-gpu-08, both show heavy page-in and repeated "ncclAllReduce timeout" messages in dmesg.

priya: suggest isolate those two nodes from the pool with a live drain to stop client traffic before a rolling restart.

tom: can we avoid full restart? maybe a remap of tensor partitions will rebalance without restart. we have a local rebalance utility that can do a non-disruptive shard move using streaming copy. risk: causes extra NCCL traffic while copying.

rachel: given current load, safer to drain then restart GPU agent on both. initiating cordon + drain now.

rachel: ```bash
# cordon and drain
kubectl cordon us-east2-gpu-07
kubectl drain us-east2-gpu-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=300s
```

rachel: node 07 drained at 1775000180. restarting runtime-agent and gpu driver. will bring back as NotReady until health checks pass.

pagerduty-bot: suppressing non-critical alerts in us-east-2 for 15m during mitigation window.

cs-bot: noticed ~1.8k failed requests for customer-x (vector search) and elevated latency for customer-y (conversational). CS notified customers with interim note.

priya: after node 07 reboot and driver restart, NCCL stalls dropped ~65% cluster-wide. node 08 still elevated; scheduling same procedure.

rachel: drain node 08 now. restarting at 1775000305.

rachel: node 08 back at 1775000410, health checks green, NVMe latency back to baseline. continuous batching disabled kept tail latencies reasonable.

tom: root cause analysis so far: the new min_chunk_strategy allowed near-zero shard assignments under skewed key hashes which produced severe partition skew (one rank owning ~50% keys). That rank became a hotspot: KV cache grew fast -> spilled to NVMe -> increased page-in -> longer NCCL allreduce -> global stalls.

priya: actions: 1) rollback min_chunk_strategy change (hotfix PR ready: https://git.internal/runtime/pull/4890). 2) add safety guard in allocator: if any rank >25% of keys trigger automatic remap. 3) add telemetry: per-shard key histogram + NVMe page-in alarm. 4) doc runbook update for draining vs live rebalance decision tree.

rachel: I triggered rollback to previous allocator on a canary subset (5% traffic) at 1775000460. canary stable for 3 minutes, no NCCL warnings. proceeding to rollout.

pagerduty-bot: severity downgraded to S2 at 1775000500.

dan: collecting kernel logs and SMART outputs for postmortem. attaching links to artifacts: https://internal.artifacts/1775000000/nvme-logs.tar.gz

cs-bot: final customer update: customers impacted saw transient errors and latency spikes; no data corruption; engineering is rolling a permanent fix and will follow up with a postmortem.

oncall-weekend: acknowledged handoff at 1775000525. will monitor dashboards and confirm stable for 1h.

priya: follow-ups assigned: roll-forward hotfix PR (tom), add auto-remap guard (priya), enhance telemetry (rachel), customer outreach (cs-bot). postmortem scheduled today 15:00 UTC.

rachel: INCIDENT RESOLVED at 1775000600. all metrics nominal. owners: @tom (runtime allocator), @rachel (oncall), @priya (sre). please add timeline and impact numbers to the postmortem doc. :white_check_mark:
